statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Post-ISM stress is extreme, while accessible delayed NQ evidence remains two-sided rather than a verified persistent no-retracement path.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the blocking threshold; escalation would require observed persistent extension, weak retracements, or stronger aligned cross-asset confirmation.
headline: WATCH as strong ISM and oil risk meet two-sided NQ structure
body: August ISM Services rose to 55.4 with new orders at 60.9 and prices paid at 72.6, while oil stayed near six-week highs on renewed U.S.-Iran/Hormuz risk. Accessible delayed NQ near 29,224 remained below the earlier session high near 29,293, so the observed path did not establish persistent mean-reversion failure.

lookbackSummary: Published Tail moved from WATCH late in the prior U.S. session to low overnight, rose through today’s macro sequence, and reached WATCH at 14:00 UTC. The 2026-09-02 22:00 UTC slot remains unavailable.
outlookSummary: Post-ISM absorption is the immediate checkpoint. Tail can ease if two-way trade persists; Hammack’s 19:00 UTC remarks are a medium checkpoint, while Friday’s 12:30 UTC Employment Situation is the next high-Stress window. WATCH does not assume a future directional outcome.

forecast.analysis: August ISM Services surprised higher at 55.4, but delayed NQ near 29,224 remains below the earlier session high near 29,293 and well above the 29,075 low. The observed path is still two-sided, so Tail is WATCH rather than blocked.
drivers: Delayed NQ remains below the earlier session high
Oil and Hormuz risk keep Stress extreme

forecast.analysis: If the first post-ISM hour continues to produce meaningful counter-swings rather than repeated extension, Tail returns to low even though services inflation and oil keep Stress extreme.
drivers: Retracement quality after the services surprise

forecast.analysis: A low-Tail base case requires the ISM repricing to remain rotational. A renewed move that holds a fresh extreme through shallow pullbacks would be the main escalation condition.
Ahead of Hammack’s later remarks, Tail stays low if index pushes continue to retrace. Event proximity raises Stress without establishing a directional path by itself.
Hammack’s scheduled opening remarks make this an event checkpoint. Tail remains low unless the subsequent NQ response becomes persistent and poorly retraced.
If the speaker window is absorbed through two-way trade, Tail remains low. Persistent cross-asset alignment with a fresh NQ extreme would be the contrary condition.
Into the late U.S. session, Tail stays low under orderly rotation. Friday payroll proximity keeps Stress elevated even without a one-way closing structure.
Post-close liquidity can widen moves, but Tail remains low unless futures develop sustained directional efficiency without meaningful counter-swings.
Early overnight risk is dominated by thinner liquidity and geopolitical headlines. Tail stays low unless a fresh shock produces sustained extension.
The overnight base case remains low Tail if price discovery stays balanced. Oil-related inflation risk keeps Stress high ahead of payrolls.
With no scheduled U.S. release in this hour, Tail stays low unless futures begin a persistent trend with shallow retracements.
drivers: No major U.S. release this hour

forecast.analysis: Tail remains low if the Asia-to-Europe handoff is orderly. A geopolitical discontinuity or one-way futures extension would be the main invalidation.
European participation can increase range, but a larger move alone does not raise Tail. Persistence and failed retracements remain the required evidence.
As European cash trade develops, Tail remains low under two-sided index structure. Cross-asset alignment would matter only if accompanied by persistent NQ direction.
Payroll anticipation begins to increase event sensitivity. Tail stays low unless pre-release positioning itself becomes directionally persistent.
U.S. premarket liquidity starts to improve. Tail remains low while pushes retrace, although Stress stays extreme into the employment report.
Pre-NFP repositioning can widen futures swings. Tail stays low if those swings remain reversible rather than extending through failed pullbacks.
With four hours to payrolls, Tail is still low but event sensitivity rises. A persistent pre-release drift would be the condition for WATCH.
WATCH reflects tighter proximity to payrolls, not an assumed release outcome. Tail would stay capped if futures remain rotational and cross-assets conflict.
Two and a half hours before payrolls, Stress is extreme and Tail is WATCH. Future directional alignment is not assumed; sustained pre-release extension would be the escalation test.

The final full hour before payrolls carries WATCH-level Tail because liquidity and positioning can become fragile. A block would still require future evidence of persistent price structure, not event importance alone.

This hour contains the scheduled 12:30 UTC Employment Situation. Tail is WATCH before the release; any higher state would depend on the observed post-release path, retracement quality and cross-asset alignment.
The first full post-payroll hour is conditional. WATCH persists while price discovery is unsettled; meaningful retracements would lower Tail, while repeated extension would raise it.
By the second post-payroll hour, Tail is forecast to ease if discovery becomes two-sided. Continued extreme-holding with failed pullbacks would invalidate that easing.

forecastDetail.comment: Strong ISM and oil keep Stress extreme, but delayed NQ remains inside the earlier two-sided range; mapped state stays WATCH.
Tail returns to low if post-ISM trading continues to show meaningful counter-swings rather than repeated extension.

Pre-Hammack event proximity raises Stress, while Tail remains low unless pushes stop retracing.

Orderly speaker-window absorption keeps Tail low; persistent aligned cross-asset direction would be the contrary condition.
